problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}(2x+3)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{C}{2x+3},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by ${x}^{2}(2x+3)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =Ax(2x+3)+B(2x+3)+C{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0+2 & =A(0)(2(0)+3)+B(2(0)+3)+C(0)^{2} \\ 2 & =3B \\ B & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-\frac{3}{2}$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}+2 & =A(-\frac{3}{2})(2(-\frac{3}{2})+3)+B(2(-\frac{3}{2})+3)+C{(-\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{2} & =C(\frac{9}{4}) \\ C & =\frac{4}{18} \\ C & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=1$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1+2 & =A(1)(2(1)+3)+(\frac{2}{3})(2(1)+3)+(\frac{2}{9})(1)^{2} \\ 3 & =5A+\frac{10}{3}+\frac{2}{9} \\ 3 & =5A+\frac{32}{9} \\ 5A & =-\frac{5}{9} \\ A & =-\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =-\frac{1}{9}\cdot \frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{9} \\  & =-\frac{4}{243}.\end{aligned}
$$
